problems.title: Use one temporary variable for repeated expressions
problems.question: Simplify $[1/(x-y+1)+1/(x-y+2)]\,[(x-y)^2+2x-2y+1]/(2x-2y+3)$.
problems.idea: Set t=x-y and factor the numerator.
steps: Multiply by (t+1)²/(2t+3) and cancel the common factors.

problems.title: A positive radical binomial cancels
problems.question: Evaluate $\sqrt{5-2\sqrt6}(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)^{-1}$.
problems.idea: The radicand is the square of the denominator.
steps: Divide by the same nonzero number to get 1.

problems.title: Count roots after clearing denominators
problems.question: How many real solutions has $1/(x+1)-1/(x+2)=2/(x^2-4)$?
problems.idea: Combine the left side and keep all forbidden values.
steps: Cross-multiply on the allowed domain: x-2=2(x+1).
This gives x=-4, which is allowed.

problems.title: Two possible feet on a line
problems.question: A,B lie on a line with AB=15 cm. Point C is 6 cm from the line and 10 cm from A. Find BC.
problems.idea: The perpendicular foot can lie on either side of A.
formulas: Pythagoras: horizontal distance from A to the foot=√(10²-6²)=8.
steps: Put A=(0,0),B=(15,0). Then C has coordinates (8,±6) or (-8,±6).
problems.answer: BC=√85 cm or √565 cm; only √85 is listed.
problems.note: The question does not locate C’s perpendicular foot relative to A and B, so both distances satisfy its data.

problems.title: A quadratic with consecutive parameter roots
problems.question: For x²-(2a+1)x+a+a²=0, find the roots and the absolute difference between them.
problems.idea: Factor using a and a+1.
steps: The roots are x=a and x=a+1.
This holds for every real a.

problems.title: Incircle height in a right trapezoid
problems.question: A right trapezoid has inradius 6 and acute angle 30°. Find its midline.
problems.idea: The base separation is twice the inradius, and tangency relates base and leg sums.
formulas: h=2r; slanted leg=h/sinθ; a+b=sum of legs for a tangential quadrilateral.
steps: The height and perpendicular leg are 12.
The base sum is 12+24=36, so the midline is 36/2=18.

problems.title: A positive lower bound prevents any roots
problems.question: How many real solutions has (x²+1)²+(x²+1)-1=0?
problems.idea: The substituted quantity is at least 1.
steps: The entire left side is at least 1 for every real x.
It can therefore never equal zero.

problems.title: The angle-bisector theorem inside a parallelogram
problems.question: A parallelogram has adjacent sides 10 and 5 cm. In what ratio does the bisector of an acute angle divide the opposite diagonal?
problems.idea: The two sides and that diagonal form a triangle.
formulas: An internal angle bisector divides the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides.
steps: Draw the triangle using the two sides of lengths 10 and 5 at the bisected angle.
Its opposite side is the diagonal joining the other endpoints.
The diagonal pieces have ratio 10:5=2:1, or 1:2 if read in the opposite direction.

problems.title: Combine chord power with tangent-secant power
problems.question: From external M, tangent MA=2√5. Chord AD=10 contains K with AK=6. A secant from M through K meets the circle at B,C, with KC=8. Find the external secant part.
problems.idea: First find the other chord part through K.
steps: If the external part is t=MB, then MC=t+11 and t(t+11)=MA²=20.
problems.note: None of the listed integer choices equals the result from the printed lengths. The usual order M-B-K-C is used; K lies inside the circle on chord AD.

problems.title: Reject an extraneous root from squaring
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{2x+6}=x-1$.
problems.idea: The right side must be nonnegative.
formulas: √u=v requires v≥0, and squaring must be checked in the original equation.
steps: The candidate -1 violates x≥1. At x=5, both sides equal 4.

problems.title: Incircle of a 60-degree rhombus
problems.question: A rhombus has a side equal to one diagonal, both 4 cm. Find its inradius.
problems.idea: The equal diagonal forms an equilateral triangle, giving acute angle 60°.

problems.title: A rectangle with one side half a diagonal
problems.question: A rectangle’s circumradius is 2√3. Its shorter side is half the diagonal. Find the longer side.
problems.idea: The diagonal is the circumdiameter.
steps: The diagonal is d=4√3 and the short side is a=2√3.

problems.title: Check that real roots exist before using Vieta
problems.question: For which real a does x²+ax+a²+2=0 have real roots x₁,x₂ satisfying 3x₁+3x₂+x₁x₂=0?
problems.idea: The existence condition fails for every a.
formulas: A real quadratic needs discriminant D≥0.
steps: Here D=a²-4(a²+2)=-3a²-8<0 for every real a.
Therefore it has no real roots at all, so none can satisfy the additional condition.
Using only Vieta would suggest a²-3a+2=0, but its values 1 and 2 still have negative discriminants.

problems.title: Angle between two tangents from the origin
problems.question: Find the angle between the two tangent rays from the origin to (x-6)²=9-y².
problems.idea: Use the right triangle formed by the centre, origin and a tangent point.
formulas: A radius to a tangent point is perpendicular to the tangent; sin(half-angle)=radius/centre distance.
steps: The circle is centred at (6,0) with radius 3. Its centre is 6 from the origin.
The half-angle is 30°, so the full angle is 60°.

problems.title: A root is constrained to an interval
problems.question: The solution of 3x+1-a=2x+3a-1 belongs to [-1,2]. Find a.
problems.idea: First express x in terms of a.

problems.title: An absolute-value equation with one valid case
problems.question: Find the sum of the absolute values of the roots of |x+2|=3-2x.
problems.idea: Split at x=-2 and check each case’s interval.
formulas: For x≥-2, |x+2|=x+2; for x<-2 it equals -x-2.
steps: If x≥-2, x+2=3-2x gives x=1/3, which is valid.
If x<-2, -x-2=3-2x gives x=5, outside that case and invalid.
The only root has absolute value 1/3.

problems.title: Coordinates of an internal division point
problems.question: A=(0,5),B=(10,0), and AC:CB=3:2. Find C.
problems.idea: Move three fifths of the way from A to B.
steps: Three fifths of this displacement is (6,-3).

problems.title: Perpendicular diagonals determine a trapezoid’s midline
problems.question: A trapezoid has perpendicular diagonals of lengths 60 and 80 cm. Find its midline.
problems.idea: Orient one diagonal upward and the other downward so that their vertical components cancel.
formulas: For perpendicular vectors of lengths p,q, their sum has length √(p²+q²); midline=base sum/2.
steps: Orient the first diagonal from the lower-left vertex to the upper-right vertex, and the second from the upper-left to the lower-right. Their vector sum is horizontal and equals the sum of the bases.
Because the diagonals are perpendicular, this length is √(60²+80²)=100.

problems.title: Convert an absolute-value inequality to two bounds
problems.question: Solve |1-x|<2x+1.
problems.idea: Both inequalities -v<u<v must hold.
formulas: |u|<v iff -v<u<v; these bounds also force v>0.
steps: The first gives x>-2 and the second gives x>0.
Their intersection is x>0; here the right side is positive as required.

problems.title: Circumradius from the two shorter sides
problems.question: An obtuse triangle has angles 30° and 45°. Its two shorter sides sum to 5+5√2. Find its circumradius.
problems.idea: The two shorter sides are opposite the two smaller angles.
formulas: Extended sine rule: side opposite θ=2R sinθ.

problems.title: Binary representation of fifty-nine
problems.question: Write 59 in binary.
problems.idea: Subtract the largest powers of two.

problems.title: Appending a digit gives an equation
problems.question: Appending digit 4 to a positive integer gives a number 20 less than its square. Find the sum of the original integer’s digits.
problems.idea: Appending 4 changes n into 10n+4.

problems.title: Distance to a point on a triangle side
problems.question: AB=4,AC=5,BC=√21. D lies on AC with AD=2. Find BD.
problems.idea: Use the cosine rule twice with the common angle A.

problems.title: A base ratio from diagonal division
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid’s diagonals divide each other in ratio 1:3. Its midline is 6 cm. Find the larger base.
problems.idea: The diagonal division ratio equals the base ratio.
steps: Write the bases as t and 3t.
Their sum is 2·6=12, so 4t=12 and t=3.

problems.title: Check a linear case as well as a double root
problems.question: For which a does ax²+(a+2)x+2=0 have exactly one distinct real solution?
problems.idea: Factor the expression and keep the case a=0.
steps: If a≠0, the roots are -1 and -2/a. They coincide exactly when a=2.
If a=0, the equation becomes 2x+2=0, with just the root -1.
There are no other cases with one distinct root.
problems.note: The choices that give only one of these values are incomplete; the combined set {0,2} is the full answer.
